elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 expressly provides that the Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: The state courts located in New York County, New York have jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Sections 28.1 and 28.2 designate the state courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: The federal courts located in New York County, New York have jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Sections 28.1 and 28.2 designate the federal courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: Jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York is exclusive.
elements.evidence: Although Sections 28.1 and 28.2 use exclusive-jurisdiction language, Section 28.2 permits either Party to seek temporary injunctive relief in another court for confidential-information or intellectual-property matters. The required exclusivity is therefore subject to an express remedy-based exception.

elements.element: The Agreement is governed by Delaware law, California law, or the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects New York law, not any accepted fallback law.

elements.element: Disputes are submitted to courts corresponding to the selected fallback law: Delaware courts for Delaware law, California courts for California law, or the courts of London for the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause designates New York County courts rather than Delaware courts, California courts, or the courts of London.

result.reason: The redline adopts New York governing law and the specified New York County courts, but the retained temporary-injunctive-relief carveout permits proceedings in another court and therefore fails the unqualified exclusive-jurisdiction requirement. No fallback law-and-court package is used. The drafting also unnecessarily duplicates the New York County jurisdiction language in Sections 28.1 and 28.2. The carveout can be harmonized as an express exception, so it does not create an irreconcilable contradiction or disturb unrelated commercial terms.
